book.title: Post-Crisis: Applied Limits
chapters_read: C:/Users/palle/Documents/GitHub/AdaResearch_46/commons/maps/QFEP_Synthesis/final.md (last chapter of qfeplaboratory, for the handover in)
C:/Users/palle/Documents/GitHub/AdaResearch_46/commons/maps/PostCrisis_Synthesis/final.md (no next sequence: 24 of 24; its teleporter is t:lab)

reading.arc: The sequence takes the museum's closing question, 'knowing the limits of formalisation, what do we build?', and answers it as a chain of design decisions the visitor can operate rather than admire: how much room a representation gives a distinction (bias), what a seating plan decides before anyone speaks (ethics), what a resolved disagreement deletes (paraconsistency), where a verdict is spoken from (situated), what a count of contributions hides and who may revise (collective), which connections a body can enter and which it can only see (rhizome), and how a body's pose and its neighbours can be changed by hand (laboratory). Each hall follows one rhythm: an instruction to press or move something, a short code excerpt introduced by 'The source makes the operation inspectable', a paragraph stating exactly what the exhibit does not establish, and a question to carry out. The visitor's own alteration in the laboratory is written to a pose record and stands again in the final hall beside the body it began from, where the ledger shows what the record kept and what it could not. The book closes by turning the question back on the maker (what would you want the record to keep next, which change do you still want to make) and by circling to the first hall's counter that was already running when we arrived.
holds: The refrain 'The source makes the operation inspectable' with a verified excerpt in six of the eight halls, always followed by a sentence about what the code does not prove (a picture of a decision, not a proof; equal spacing, not equal opportunity).

A 'what this exhibit cannot establish' paragraph in every hall: authored positions not measured embeddings; supplied percentages not calibrated probabilities; a simulation of accretion not a live editor; composed passages not a grown network; authored targets not discovered destinations.

The carried object: the hand you moved. The laboratory's released pose crosses to the final hall through AssemblyPoseRecord, and the last line ('The clock is still running') returns to Point_One's counter.
Keeping the subject constant while the frame changes: same words, less room; same subject, four verdicts; same points, other connections; same hand, another neighbour.

Every hall ends by naming the next version it would want (a named model and documented measurement, observed sightlines, a small rule table, a criterion per panel, a browsable history, a new opening in the wall, another joint, the path of the hand), so the sequence's 'return with a change' is rehearsed seven times before the final hall asks for it.

Buttons in small caps as the prose's verbs (READ, PAIR, RESOLVED, COVER, DISPUTE, VERSION, HANG AGAIN): the visitor's operations are the chapter's paragraphs, and every named control exists on the artifact's console.

hall_notes.note: Opens the sequence on the COMPRESSION handle: two coloured word groups, one lerp, and the difference between being present and being tellable-apart. The tightest chapter in the sequence; every claim matches bias_from_inside.gd, and READ hands the reader the maker's own caveat ('Both groups were chosen').

Five seating plans on one console (HEAD, CIRCLE, PAIR, WATCH, VACANT) plus the COLOUR/NEUTRAL persuasion switch. Its cadence is press-then-think, close to a guided operation, but each press earns its thought and the refusal to let geometry stand in for participation is exact.

Four authored pictures of a disagreement; the RESOLVED stump ('look down for B') is the hall's best moment. The formal paragraph on explosion is honest about the limit of the analogy, but the one citation is a bare hyperlink a headset reader cannot follow.

One subject, four verdicts, three ways of showing an address (FOOTNOTE, COVER, WITNESS). The 'dangerous to whom, under which circumstances' passage is the strongest accountability writing in the sequence. The spider is introduced in the last paragraph, after ten paragraphs that tell the reader to linger.

Two works: the helix workbench (FLOW, COLOUR, PIECE, DISPUTE, REVISE, VERSION) and the round table with no head. The counting passage is accurate to the readout but narrates a label change the reader never saw; the table's cards are described as turned toward different approaches, which the code does not build.

Cave first (the violet junction, the overcrossing you cannot turn at, the minf union that lets two volumes share an interior), grower second (one link or three, cut a busy point, the ring that does not spread). The best prose in the sequence, but the reading order is the reverse of the walk, and the opening question line is dropped.

The longest hall by 650 words: a hand you can leave too far away, an inventory finding authored targets, one rerouteable connection that makes and unmakes a loop, a ragdoll that falls, and a chair, table and lamp that pull apart. Every mechanical claim matches the scripts; the reader carries thirteen joint names with no heading to rest on.

Two bodies (blue start, amber kept) and a ledger that reads the same record; the argument that the destination survives while the gesture does not is exact and moving ('The hand has arrived. Your hand is missing.'). Closes the book by circling to the first hall's counter; one ledger sentence is garbled.

stumbles: SpeculativeComputation_Rhizome_Network: the chapter walks the cave and then 'the small grower', but the map puts the grower beside the spawn and the cave between spawn and exit, so a visitor following the text returns to the entrance and then says goodbye to the hall from its far end.

SpeculativeComputation_Situated_Computation: 'Stay with DANGEROUS. Read its 92%' is issued in a room where a biting spider notices the visitor from 14 m; the creature is only mentioned in the final paragraph.

SpeculativeComputation_Collective_Knowledge: 'some of those cards faced away' sends the reader looking for cards turned different ways; every station pad is built with position only and faces the same direction.

SpeculativeComputation_Collective_Knowledge: 'In the earlier display, a number labelled CONTRIBUTORS ... That number is now called PARTICIPATIONS' reads as a changelog; the reader has never seen an earlier display.
PostCrisis_Synthesis: 'distinguishes twelve connections from twelve unchanged connections' is not a sentence a reader can parse; the ledger prints 'retained' or 'N rerouted'.

AdvancedLaboratory_Lab_Equipment_Simulation: 1,677 words, five encounters and no heading; the head-torso-shoulder-elbow loop and its undoing ask the reader to hold thirteen names across two paragraphs.
AdvancedLaboratory_Lab_Equipment_Simulation to PostCrisis_Synthesis: 'the gold body' becomes 'an amber body' between the two halls for the same figure.
SpeculativeComputation_Paraconsistent_Engineering: the Basu and Roy citation is a hyperlink whose anchor is a whole sentence and whose paper is never named; there is nothing to click in a headset.
CriticalAlgorithms_Applied_Ethics: 'the panel stays where your hand left it' implies the visitor placed the console; it is fixed.

SpeculativeComputation_Rhizome_Network, AdvancedLaboratory_Lab_Equipment_Simulation, PostCrisis_Synthesis: the one-line question under the title that the first five halls (and QFEP_Synthesis before them) open with disappears for the last three.

keep.quote: Presence in a representation is therefore different from being represented with useful distinctions.
Equal spacing is what this loop guarantees. Equal opportunity to speak would require another kind of evidence.
Its useful first gesture is spatial: an unresolved relation can be represented without erasing the parts that made the relation difficult.
A favourable word also needs criteria; situatedness is not a licence to stop checking an appealing claim.
The table has no head. The classification still has an author.
We have not escaped geometry by drawing a network. We have acquired another place to work on it.
A body can look as though it is coming into being while it is coming into agreement with a description.
The hand has arrived. Your hand is missing.

reading.handover_in: Clean. QFEP_Synthesis ends with Self-Q ('After giving this body a name, a container and a range of responses ... Which part of the apparatus would we change next?') and then 'Post-crisis begins with representation itself. After learning to name a model's choices, ask whose distinctions those choices make clear and whose they compress.' The bias hall opens on exactly that: 'Which differences become difficult to recognise when a representation gives some words less room?' The sequence also answers the Self-Q question in its last hall ('Choose one alteration you still want to make'), so the promise is kept end to end.
reading.handover_out: There is no next sequence (24 of 24); the final hall's teleporter is t:lab and the sequence file says return_to: lab. The chapter closes the book rather than handing on: 'This is a place to turn around ... The clock is still running. There is something you wanted to make.' The clock is Point_One's frame counter ('The room's counter reads a total that began earlier'; Point_Lines: 'The clock in the first room was already running when we arrived'), so the ending deliberately loops to the first hall and leaves the request open. The only mismatch is internal to the arc: the lab's 'gold body' is the synthesis hall's 'amber body'.

tasks.title: The station cards all face one way
tasks.spec:
[encounter] SpeculativeComputation_Collective_Knowledge
Quote: “Each little instrument has its card turned towards a different approach. From where you first stood, some of those cards faced away.”
Why: _tag() sets only a position on each TextScreen pad and never a rotation, so the six station cards and the centre card all face the same direction; the reader is told to find cards turned away and cannot, and the conclusion 'There is no position from which every account addresses you at once' is untrue of the room as built.
Do: Either pass each station's angle into _tag and set tag.rotation.y so every pad faces outward from the table centre (then the sentences are true), or cut the two sentences and let 'Take a place at the rim, then walk to another' stand on the instruments themselves.

tasks.title: Drop the changelog voice from the counting passage
tasks.spec:
[prose] SpeculativeComputation_Collective_Knowledge
Quote: “In the earlier display, a number labelled CONTRIBUTORS could therefore outgrow the twelve source positions. That number is now called PARTICIPATIONS.”
Why: The reader has never seen an 'earlier display' (the CONTRIBUTORS label exists only in the original commit), so 'is now called' narrates the author's revision history instead of the readout in front of the visitor; the good point underneath (a label can turn repeated attendance into an expanding community) survives in the present tense.
Do: Recast: 'Read PARTICIPATIONS again after a VERSION. It can pass twelve, because it adds together each version's distinct sources. Call that number CONTRIBUTORS and a label has quietly turned repeated attendance into an expanding community. SOURCES counts distinct nodes in this version; EVER counts distinct nodes across versions.'
